questions.question: Before changing lanes, what should you do?

options.text: Turn your head quickly to look for other vehicles.

questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check both mirrors for traffic behind you. Just before you move, look over your shoulder to check for vehicles in your blind spot.

questions.question: What can cause distracted driving?

options.text: Talking or texting on a phone.

questions.explanation: Drivers must make many decisions while driving. Any extra activity takes your attention away from the road and creates danger.

questions.question: How can you make sure your physical condition doesn't make driving unsafe?

options.text: Stay physically fit and get regular checkups.
Learn how medicines affect your driving.
Drive only within your physical limits.

questions.explanation: Your physical condition affects how safely you drive. Know your limitations and only drive when it is safe.

questions.question: What does alcohol do?
questions.explanation: Even a small amount of alcohol harms your vision, judgment, concentration, and coordination.

questions.question: What is a sign of a drunk driver?

options.text: They drive much slower than other traffic.

questions.explanation: Signs of drunk driving include weaving, driving too slowly, jerky movements, and sudden stops.

questions.question: Why should you not follow other cars too closely?

options.text: You may not see the road between the cars.
You may not have time to stop if the car in front stops suddenly.
You may not see the turn signals.
You may not see the brake lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may not have time to stop if the car in front stops suddenly.
questions.explanation: If you follow too closely and the car ahead stops suddenly, you may not have enough time to avoid hitting it.

questions.question: What can happen when you mix alcohol with another drug?

options.text: Only the alcohol effect may weaken.

questions.explanation: Mixing alcohol with another drug can make both effects stronger. For example, one drink combined with a cold medicine might affect you like having several drinks.

questions.question: What affects braking distance?

options.text: The condition of your brakes and tires.

questions.explanation: Braking distance depends on your speed, the condition of your brakes and tires, and the road surface.

questions.question: What safety restraints work best in a crash?

options.text: Only a lap and shoulder belt.
Both a lap/shoulder belt and an airbag.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both a lap/shoulder belt and an airbag.
questions.explanation: Seat belts double your chance of surviving a crash. Airbags with seat belts provide extra protection in front-end crashes. Use both.

questions.question: What is true about drivers who drink alcohol before driving?

options.text: They always know the risks they are taking.
They cannot control their bodies, minds, or vehicles properly.
They are better drivers because they drive more carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: They cannot control their bodies, minds, or vehicles properly.
questions.explanation: Alcohol damages judgment, vision, concentration, understanding, and reaction time. Never drink any amount of alcohol before driving.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You can continue through the interchange or exit the freeway from your current lane.
You can stay in your lane and continue through the interchange.
You must exit the freeway if you stay in your current lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must exit the freeway if you stay in your current lane.
questions.explanation: An "Exit only" sign means the lane below it will exit the highway. You cannot continue straight through the interchange in that lane. You can either change lanes to go through, or you must exit the highway.

questions.question: Your brake lights tell other drivers that you:
questions.explanation: Brake lights show other drivers that you are slowing down or stopping. Your brake lights must work properly when you drive.

questions.question: On long trips, you can prevent drowsiness by:

options.text: Moving your eyes from side to side as you drive.

questions.explanation: Stop regularly on long trips to rest and stretch. Do this even if you do not feel tired yet.

questions.question: A pedestrian starts to cross in front of your vehicle. You should:

options.text: Speed up and pass in front of the pedestrian.
Stop and let the pedestrian cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the pedestrian cross.
questions.explanation: Slow down when you see pedestrians. Always be ready to stop. Give pedestrians the right-of-way, especially in crosswalks and where children are present.

questions.question: Mixing alcohol with drugs can:
questions.explanation: Mixing alcohol and drugs increases the effects of both. It is dangerous to drive after consuming either one. Mixing them together is even more dangerous.

questions.question: When turning left, drivers must yield the right-of-way to:

options.text: Other drivers already in the intersection.

questions.explanation: When turning left, yield to oncoming traffic. Always yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and other drivers already in the intersection.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is true?

options.text: Sudden weather changes mean you should change how you drive.
Slow down when driving in rain and fog.
Watch for vehicles behind you in bad weather.

questions.explanation: Adjust your driving when weather changes suddenly. Slow down in rain and fog. Watch for vehicles behind you that may be driving too fast for the conditions.

questions.question: If you leave your vehicle unattended, you must:

options.text: Lock the ignition and remove the key.

questions.explanation: When leaving your vehicle, turn off the engine, lock the ignition, remove the key, and set the parking brake.

questions.question: You are in an accident. You should:
questions.explanation: Stop your vehicle right away. Move it out of traffic if you can. Call the police and ask for an ambulance if needed. Help stop severe bleeding but do not move injured people. Wait for emergency vehicles.

questions.question: Before turning, you should:
questions.explanation: Use your turn signal 3 to 4 seconds before you turn.

questions.question: If you miss your exit on an interstate expressway, what should you do?

options.text: Get off at the next exit and come back to the exit you missed.
Roll down your window and ask the driver next to you for help.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get off at the next exit and come back to the exit you missed.
questions.explanation: Never back up or turn around on the highway. Instead, go to the next exit and safely turn around.

questions.question: What is the purpose of highway markings?

options.text: They are only found in construction zones.
They are usually red and blue in color.

questions.explanation: Highway markings give drivers important information. They help you position your vehicle correctly, show safe passing zones, and warn you about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns drivers that the divided highway is ending ahead.

questions.question: When turning or changing lanes, you must:

options.text: Always signal your intentions, even when no other traffic is visible.
Signal only if other traffic is nearby.
Signal only when driving at night.
Signal only in heavy traffic at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always signal your intentions, even when no other traffic is visible.
questions.explanation: Always signal when changing lanes, turning, or leaving a curb. Make this a habit—do not skip signaling just because you do not see other cars.

questions.question: What do speed limit signs tell you?

options.text: The possible speeds for the area
The fastest and slowest speeds you are legally allowed to drive
The speed you should drive in heavy traffic
The speed you should drive in bad weather

questions.correctAnswerText: The fastest and slowest speeds you are legally allowed to drive
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs show the legal maximum and minimum speeds for that road. The limits are for normal conditions. You must drive slower when weather, traffic, or other conditions make it necessary.

questions.question: How can stress affect your driving?

options.text: It reduces your ability to focus on driving.
It decreases your chances of having an accident.
It makes you fall asleep at the wheel.
It makes you more aware of others around you.

questions.correctAnswerText: It reduces your ability to focus on driving.
questions.explanation: Strong emotions hurt your driving ability. If you are worried, excited, scared, angry, or sad, you may not drive well. Stress reduces your focus on the road. Wait to drive until you feel calm and ready.

questions.question: When you hear a fire engine siren behind you, what must you do?

options.text: Slow down until it passes you.
Pull over to the side of the road and stop.
Speed up and take the nearest exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear an emergency vehicle siren, pull over to the side of the road and stop.

questions.question: What should you do when crossing railroad tracks?

options.text: Look both ways only when the red light is flashing.
Listen, look both ways, and cross only if it is safe.
Cross very quickly when a train is approaching.
Quickly pass under any lowering gates.

questions.correctAnswerText: Listen, look both ways, and cross only if it is safe.
questions.explanation: Railroad crossings are always dangerous. Look and listen for trains from both directions before crossing. Watch for warning signals and never cross until you are sure it is safe.

questions.question: Can you drive around or under a gate that is going up or down at a railroad crossing?

options.text: Yes, as long as a train is not too close.
Yes, if your vehicle will not damage the gate.
Yes, if you look both ways first.

questions.explanation: Flashing red lights, lowered gates, and bells mean you must stop. Do not cross the tracks until the lights and bells stop and the gates are fully raised. Never drive around or under a moving gate.

questions.question: If a flagger is directing traffic in a construction zone, what must you do?

options.text: Follow the directions given by the flagger.
Follow what other drivers are doing instead of the flagger's directions.
Assume the flagger should not be directing traffic.
Follow normal road rules as if the area was not under construction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the directions given by the flagger.
questions.explanation: Follow all directions from signs, flaggers, and police officers in construction zones. Ignoring these directions is illegal and dangerous to workers.
